edit.namespaceHint: Leave it empty to remove the default namespace.
edit.deleteHint: The context {{context}} is removed from its kubeconfig file, together with its cluster and user entries when no other context uses them.
edit.backupHint: Before writing, the file as it is now is copied next to it (.bak- and the time).
edit.realFile: The path is a link. The change is written to the file it points to: {{path}}
edit.backupAt: Before writing, the file as it is now is copied to {{path}} (with the time of the change). Older copies made by Sextant are deleted (copies kept: {{max}}).
edit.currentContextUnset: The current context is left unset: kubectl uses no cluster until you choose one.
edit.currentContextElsewhere: These KUBECONFIG files name the old context as the current one, and Sextant may not edit them. They keep the old name, which then names no context:
edit.commentsLost: The file has comments. They are not kept when the file is written.
edit.layoutChanges: The file is written in a standard YAML layout: quoting and indentation may change.
edit.notWritable: Sextant may not edit this file. Allow it for this kubeconfig in Settings → Clusters first.
edit.written: Saved. The previous file was copied to {{path}}
edit.disconnected: Clusters whose context was renamed or deleted were disconnected.
edit.conflict: The file changed after the preview. Look at the change again.

merge.title: Merge kubeconfig files
merge.hint: The contexts, clusters and users of the chosen files are copied into Sextant's own kubeconfig file. A name that is already taken gets a suffix (-2, -3). The chosen files are not changed.
merge.dialogTitle: Choose a kubeconfig file to merge

sources.warningTitle: Allow Sextant to edit this file?
sources.warning: Sextant will be able to rename, change and delete contexts in this file, each time after you confirm a preview of the change. The file is copied (.bak- and the time) before every write. Other programs, such as kubectl and cloud CLIs, use this file too.
sources.backups: A copy is made before each write: {{path}} (copies kept: {{max}})

expiry.daysHint: Client certificates and tokens whose expiry the kubeconfig tells. A user who logs in through a program is not checked.
expiry.exec: This user logs in through {{command}}; when the login expires is known only after it.
expiry.provider: This user logs in through the {{command}} auth provider; when the login expires is known only after it.
expiry.oidcRefresh: The token is renewed through its OIDC provider.
expiry.unreadable: The credentials named in the kubeconfig cannot be read.

validate.title: Kubeconfig check
validate.hint: These problems were found without connecting. A context with a problem may fail to connect.

code.notYaml: The file is not valid YAML.
code.notYamlAt: The file is not valid YAML (line {{line}}, column {{column}}).
code.notKubeconfig: The file is YAML but not a kubeconfig.
code.currentContextMissing: The current context {{subject}} does not exist.
code.noServer: The cluster has no server address.
code.badServerUrl: The server address {{subject}} is not an https:// or http:// URL.
code.caUnreadable: The certificate authority is not a valid certificate.
code.clientCertificateUnreadable: The client certificate is not a valid certificate.
code.execNotFound: The login program {{subject}} is not installed or not in PATH.
code.insecureTls: The server's certificate is not verified (insecure-skip-tls-verify).
